healthy.symptoms: Vibrant chlorophyll green coloration, crisp margins, regular vascular venation. Zero foliar lesions, bacterial ooze, water-soaking, or insect puncture damage observed.
healthy.cultural: Maintain scheduled drip or furrow irrigation, balanced split N-P-K nutrient application, and regular bi-weekly field scouting.
healthy.biological: Apply prophylactic soil application of Trichoderma viride (@ 2.5 kg/ha enriched with 250 kg FYM) during final land preparation.
healthy.chemical: No chemical intervention needed. Avoid unnecessary prophylactic fungicide or pesticide spraying to conserve beneficial field parasitoids.
healthy.management: Maintain balanced N-P-K nutrient application, scheduled irrigation, and regular bi-weekly field scouting.

rice blast.symptoms: Spindle-shaped elliptical foliar lesions with grayish-white centers and dark brown to reddish-brown margins. Severe collar rot on flag leaves and blackish necrotic lesions at panicle neck causing 'neck blast' and complete spikelet sterility.
rice blast.cultural: Avoid excessive split nitrogen doses (>120 kg N/ha in single dose); drain field standing water intermittently; burn or deeply plow infected stubbles; avoid late planting.
rice blast.biological: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens 1% WP (@ 10g/kg seed), followed by seedling root dip (@ 2.5 kg/ha) and foliar spray (@ 5g/L) at 45 days after transplanting.
rice blast.chemical: Seed treatment with Tricyclazole 75% WP (@ 2g/kg seed). Foliar spray of Tricyclazole 75% WP (@ 0.6 g/L or 120 g/acre) or Isoprothiolane 40% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L) or Kasugamycin 3% SL (@ 2.5 ml/L) at initial lesion appearance.
rice blast.etl: 2 to 5% leaf area infected with spindle lesions, or neck infection initiation.
rice blast.management: Seed treatment with Tricyclazole 75 WP (@ 2g/kg). Avoid excessive nitrogen. Spray Tricyclazole 75 WP (@ 0.6 g/L) or Isoprothiolane 40 EC (@ 1.5 ml/L) at early booting.

rice bacterial blight.organism: Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae - Gram-negative bacterium
rice bacterial blight.symptoms: Water-soaked translucent stripes starting from leaf tips and margins, expanding into broad wavy yellow-to-straw-colored blights. In early mornings, milky to amber-colored bacterial ooze droplets appear on leaf surface drying into microscopic encrusted beads (kresek phase causes total seedling wilting).
rice bacterial blight.cultural: Drain excess stagnant field water; ensure field sanitation; avoid clipping seedling tips at transplanting; delay top dressing of nitrogenous fertilizers until disease ceases.
rice bacterial blight.biological: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens (@ 10g/kg); foliar spray of fresh cow dung slurry extract (20%) or neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%).
rice bacterial blight.chemical: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L or 500 g/acre) tank-mixed with Streptocycline (Streptomycin sulphate + Tetracycline @ 100 ppm, i.e., 6g per 60 liters of water) or Plantomycin (@ 1 g/L). Repeat after 12-15 days.
rice bacterial blight.etl: 1-2 infected leaves per hill during active tillering to boot leaf stage.
rice bacterial blight.management: Drain excess water. Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) mixed with Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm) at initial leaf margin yellowing.

rice brown spot.symptoms: Numerous circular to oval dark brown spots (0.5 to 1.5 cm) on leaves with yellowish halo surrounding greyish centers. In severe cases, causes blighting of seedling coleoptile and dark discoloration of grain husks ('dirty panicle').
rice brown spot.cultural: Amend soil with potassium (K2O @ 50 kg/ha) and organic compost to correct nutritional deficiency ('poor man’s disease'); use certified healthy certified seeds.
rice brown spot.biological: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride 1% WP (@ 10g/kg seed) + soil application of enriched compost.
rice brown spot.chemical: Seed treatment with Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 3g/kg). Foliar spray of Propiconazole 25% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2 g/L) or Edifenphos 50% EC (@ 1 ml/L) at booting.
rice brown spot.etl: 2-3 brown spots per leaf on 10% of hills.
rice brown spot.management: Correct soil potash deficiency. Spray Propiconazole 25 EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2 g/L).

rice sheath blight.symptoms: Oval or oblong greenish-gray water-soaked lesions on leaf sheaths near water line. Lesions enlarge with irregular dark reddish-brown margins, spreading upward to flag leaf blades forming a 'banded blight' appearance.
rice sheath blight.cultural: Avoid close planting (keep optimum 20x15 cm spacing); remove floating organic sclerotial debris during puddle land prep; reduce nitrogen doses.
rice sheath blight.biological: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens (@ 2.5 kg/ha) mixed in 500 L water at 30 and 45 days after transplanting.
rice sheath blight.chemical: Spray Hexaconazole 5% EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Validamycin 3% L (@ 2.5 ml/L) or Thifluzamide 24% SC (@ 0.75 ml/L or 150 ml/acre) targeting lower canopy sheaths.
rice sheath blight.etl: 5-10% of hills affected at maximum tillering to panicle initiation.
rice sheath blight.management: Maintain optimum spacing. Spray Hexaconazole 5 EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Validamycin 3 L (@ 2.5 ml/L) directing spray nozzle towards sheath bases.

rice false smut.symptoms: Individual grains transform into large, velvety greenish-orange to dark olive-green pulverulent spore balls (smut balls), covered by a membrane that ruptures to release powdery chlamydospores.
rice false smut.cultural: Use certified clean disease-free seeds; avoid excess nitrogen application especially at flowering stage; destroy smutted panicles in plastic bags.
rice false smut.biological: Foliar application of Trichoderma viride (@ 2.5 kg/ha) at early boot leaf stage.
rice false smut.chemical: Foliar spray of Copper Hydroxide 77% WP (@ 2 g/L) or Propiconazole 25% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Trifloxystrobin 25% + Tebuconazole 50% WG (@ 0.4 g/L) at booting stage (before flowering).
rice false smut.etl: Presence of individual infected smut balls in 2% of panicles.
rice false smut.management: Apply Propiconazole 25 EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Copper Hydroxide (@ 2 g/L) strictly at boot leaf stage before panicle emergence.

rice hispa.symptoms: Adult beetles scrape upper leaf epidermis producing parallel white transparent streaks; larvae mine between leaf epidermal layers causing blistered translucent blotches and whole leaf withering.
rice hispa.cultural: Clip top tips of seedling leaves prior to transplanting to eliminate hispa egg batches; pass a kerosene-soaked rope across canopy in flooded field.
rice hispa.biological: Conserve eulophid larval parasitoids; spray Neem oil 1500 ppm (@ 3 ml/L).
rice hispa.chemical: Foliar spray of Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 2.5 ml/L) or Quinalphos 25% EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Triazophos 40% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L).
rice hispa.etl: 1 adult hispa or 1 damaged leaf per hill.
rice hispa.management: Clip seedling tips before transplanting. Spray Chlorpyrifos 20 EC (@ 2.5 ml/L) or Quinalphos 25 EC (@ 2 ml/L).

rice curvularia spot.symptoms: Small brown oval spots with diffuse yellow margins on leaf blades; glume discoloration and grain spottedness causing grain chalkiness.
rice curvularia spot.cultural: Ensure balanced nutrition with adequate potassium; maintain timely harvest to prevent post-maturity field weathering.
rice curvularia spot.chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2 g/L) or Carbendazim 50% WP (@ 1 g/L) at 50% flowering.
rice curvularia spot.management: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2 g/L) or Carbendazim 50 WP (@ 1 g/L) during panicle emergence.

asiatic rice borer.organism: Chilo suppressalis / Scirpophaga incertulas (Rice Stem Borer complex)
asiatic rice borer.symptoms: Larvae bore into central tillers: during vegetative phase produces dried central shoots known as 'deadhearts'; during flowering phase produces completely bleached, empty, erect panicles known as 'whiteheads'.
asiatic rice borer.cultural: Clip seedling leaf tips before transplanting to remove egg masses; synchronous community planting; harvest close to ground level and plow stubble.
asiatic rice borer.biological: Release egg parasitoids Trichogramma japonicum (@ 100,000 to 150,000 wasps/ha) 6 times starting from 15 days after transplanting; install pheromone traps (@ 8 traps/ha).
asiatic rice borer.chemical: Apply Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% GR (@ 4 kg/acre) or Cartap Hydrochloride 4% G (@ 10 kg/acre) in standing water, or foliar spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (@ 0.3 ml/L or 60 ml/acre).
asiatic rice borer.etl: 2 egg masses/m² or 5% deadhearts at vegetative stage; 2% whiteheads at flowering.
asiatic rice borer.management: Install pheromone traps (8/ha). Apply Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Cartap Hydrochloride 4G (@ 10 kg/acre).

rice yellow stem borer.organism: Scirpophaga incertulas - Monophagous Lepidopteran stem borer
rice yellow stem borer.symptoms: Deadhearts in vegetative tillers and whiteheads with chaffy grain during reproductive booting/flowering.
rice yellow stem borer.cultural: Destroy stubbles after harvest; install light traps (1/ha) to monitor adult moths; clip seedling tips.
rice yellow stem borer.biological: Release Trichogramma japonicum (@ 1.5 lakh/ha) weekly; deploy sex pheromone lure traps.
rice yellow stem borer.chemical: Broadcast Cartap Hydrochloride 4G (@ 10 kg/acre) or spray Fipronil 5% SC (@ 2 ml/L) or Flubendiamide 39.35% SC (@ 0.25 ml/L).
rice yellow stem borer.etl: 5% deadhearts or 1 egg mass per 10 hills.
rice yellow stem borer.management: Deploy pheromone traps. Apply Fipronil 5 SC (@ 2 ml/L) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (@ 0.3 ml/L).

rice white stem borer.symptoms: Central shoot withering (deadheart) and panicle bleaching (whitehead).
rice white stem borer.cultural: Maintain continuous shallow flooding; destroy stubble; clip tips of seedlings.
rice white stem borer.biological: Trichogramma japonicum release (@ 1.5 lakh/ha); conserve larval braconid parasitoids.
rice white stem borer.chemical: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Cartap Hydrochloride 50% SP (@ 2 g/L).
rice white stem borer.management: Spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Cartap Hydrochloride 50 SP (@ 2 g/L).

yellow rice borer.symptoms: Deadheart in vegetative crop, whitehead at heading stage with hollowed stem interior.
yellow rice borer.cultural: Synchronized planting, avoid high N fertilizer, light traps.
yellow rice borer.biological: Release Trichogramma japonicum (@ 1.5 lakh/ha) at weekly intervals.
yellow rice borer.chemical: Cartap Hydrochloride 4G (@ 10 kg/acre) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (@ 0.3 ml/L).
yellow rice borer.management: Use pheromone traps (8/ha) and spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (@ 0.3 ml/L).

brown plant hopper.symptoms: Nymphs and adults congregate at base of rice hills above water line, sucking sap. Infested plants turn yellow and dry up in circular patches displaying characteristic 'hopperburn'; secretes sticky honeydew fostering sooty mold.
brown plant hopper.cultural: Provide alleyways (30 cm gap after every 2 meters); alternate wetting and drying (AWD) to deprive hoppers of humid microclimate; avoid synthetic pyrethroids which cause resurgence.
brown plant hopper.biological: Conserve mirid bugs (Cyrtorhinus lividipennis) and spiders (Lycosa pseudoannulata); apply entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium anisopliae (@ 5g/L).
brown plant hopper.chemical: Foliar spray directed strictly at stem base: Triflumezopyrim 10% SC (@ 0.5 ml/L or 94 ml/acre) or Pymetrozine 50% WG (@ 0.6 g/L or 120 g/acre) or Dinotefuran 20% SG (@ 0.4 g/L).
brown plant hopper.etl: 1-2 insects per tiller during vegetative stage; 2-5 insects per tiller after panicle emergence.
brown plant hopper.management: Practice Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD). Spray Triflumezopyrim 10 SC (@ 0.5 ml/L) or Pymetrozine 50 WG (@ 0.6 g/L) directly into stem base.

white backed plant hopper.symptoms: White adult diamond streak on thorax; suck phloem sap at hill bases producing leaf orange-yellowing and hopperburn patches.
white backed plant hopper.cultural: AWD irrigation; avoid high split N; maintain proper crop spacing.
white backed plant hopper.biological: Conserve Lycosa predatory wolf spiders; spray Metarhizium anisopliae (@ 5g/L).
white backed plant hopper.chemical: Spray Pymetrozine 50% WG (@ 0.6 g/L) or Dinotefuran 20% SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Buprofezin 25% SC (@ 1.5 ml/L).
white backed plant hopper.management: Drain water for 3-4 days. Spray Pymetrozine 50 WG (@ 0.6 g/L) or Dinotefuran 20 SG (@ 0.4 g/L).

small brown plant hopper.symptoms: Sap feeding at stem bases; vector of Rice Stripe Virus and black-streaked dwarf disease.
small brown plant hopper.cultural: Eliminate alternate grassy hosts; AWD water management.
small brown plant hopper.chemical: Dinotefuran 20% SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Triflumezopyrim 10% SC (@ 0.5 ml/L).
small brown plant hopper.management: Spray Dinotefuran 20 SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Triflumezopyrim 10 SC (@ 0.5 ml/L).

rice gall midge.organism: Orseolia oryzae - Cecidomyiid gall midge fly
rice gall midge.symptoms: Maggot feeds at the growing tip inside leaf sheath, transforming the tiller shoot into a hollow, tubular, silvery-white cylindrical gall resembling an onion leaf ('silver shoot' or 'onion shoot'), preventing panicle formation.
rice gall midge.cultural: Early transplanting to escape peak midge emergence; avoid excessive vegetative nitrogen application; light traps.
rice gall midge.biological: Conserve platygastrid larval parasitoids (Platygaster oryzae); spray NSKE 5%.
rice gall midge.chemical: Apply Fipronil 0.3% GR (@ 7 kg/acre) or Chlorpyrifos 10% G (@ 4 kg/acre) or foliar spray Fipronil 5% SC (@ 2 ml/L).
rice gall midge.etl: 1 silver shoot per hill or 5% affected tillers in endemic areas.
rice gall midge.management: Apply Fipronil 0.3% GR (@ 7 kg/acre) in nursery/field or foliar spray Fipronil 5 SC (@ 2 ml/L).

rice roller.organism: Cnaphalocrocis medinalis - Rice Leaf Folder / Leaf Roller
rice roller.symptoms: Larvae fold leaves longitudinally with silk threads and feed on green mesophyll tissue inside the tube, leaving longitudinal white papery streaks across the leaf canopy.
rice roller.cultural: Avoid close spacing and shading; avoid excessive nitrogen doses; use bamboo poles to dislodge larvae.
rice roller.biological: Release Trichogramma chilonis egg parasitoids (@ 1.5 lakh/ha) thrice; spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt @ 1.5 g/L).
rice roller.chemical: Foliar spray of Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (@ 0.3 ml/L or 60 ml/acre) or Flubendiamide 39.35% SC (@ 0.25 ml/L) or Cartap Hydrochloride 50% SP (@ 2 g/L).
rice roller.etl: 1-2 damaged folded leaves per hill with live larvae.
rice roller.management: Release Trichogramma (@ 1.5 lakh/ha). Spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Flubendiamide 39.35 SC (@ 0.25 ml/L).

rice caterpillar.symptoms: Larvae march in massive armies across flooded fields, voraciously devouring seedlings and leaves down to the water surface overnight.
rice caterpillar.cultural: Trench around field bunds with water and kerosene to trap marching caterpillars; release ducks in flooded fields.
rice caterpillar.biological: Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (@ 2 g/L) or Beauveria bassiana (@ 5 g/L).
rice caterpillar.chemical: Dust field with Malathion 5% dust (@ 10 kg/acre) or foliar spray Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 2.5 ml/L) or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG (@ 0.4 g/L).
rice caterpillar.management: Dig peripheral trenches. Spray Chlorpyrifos 20 EC (@ 2.5 ml/L) or Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG (@ 0.4 g/L) during late afternoon.

rice skipper.symptoms: Larva ties leaf edges together forming tubular shelters and feeds from the leaf edge inward, creating irregular scalloped defoliation.
rice skipper.cultural: Remove broad-leaved grass weeds along bunds; handpick visible larval tubes.
rice skipper.biological: Conserve braconid and chalcid parasitoids; spray NSKE 5%.
rice skipper.chemical: Spray Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Quinalphos 25% EC (@ 2 ml/L).
rice skipper.management: Handpick folded leaf cases. Spray Quinalphos 25 EC (@ 2 ml/L) if extensive.

rice stemfly.organism: Atherigona oryzae (Rice Shoot Fly / Stem Fly)
rice stemfly.symptoms: Maggots feed on growing point of young seedlings within 20 days of germination producing deadhearts.
rice stemfly.cultural: Sow seeds immediately after monsoon arrival; increase seed rate by 10-15%.
rice stemfly.chemical: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid 70% WS (@ 3 g/kg seed) or spray Thiamethoxam 25% WG (@ 0.3 g/L).
rice stemfly.management: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid 70 WS (@ 3 g/kg) or spray Thiamethoxam 25 WG (@ 0.3 g/L).

rice water weevil.symptoms: Adults chew narrow longitudinal slit-like scars on upper leaf epidermis; larvae (root-maggots) feed underwater pruning root system leading to stunted yellowed plants that lodge easily.
rice water weevil.cultural: Drain standing water for 4-5 days to desiccate root-feeding larvae; early uniform planting.
rice water weevil.chemical: Apply Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% GR (@ 4 kg/acre) or Carbofuran 3G (@ 10 kg/acre) into water.
rice water weevil.etl: 1 adult per hill or root pruning noticeable on 10% hills.
rice water weevil.management: Intermittent field drainage to suppress larvae. Apply Chlorantraniliprole 0.4 GR (@ 4 kg/acre).

tomato early blight.symptoms: Concentric dark brown to black rings forming characteristic 'target-board' lesions on older lower leaves, surrounded by a distinct chlorotic yellow halo. Causes dark sunken collar rot lesions at stem base and sunken black leathery rot on fruit stem end.
tomato early blight.cultural: Follow 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops; maintain wide 60x45 cm plant spacing; drip irrigation instead of overhead sprinklers; remove and burn lower diseased leaves.
tomato early blight.biological: Seed treatment with Trichoderma harzianum 1% WP (@ 10g/kg); foliar spray with Pseudomonas fluorescens (@ 5g/L) or Ampelomyces quisqualis.
tomato early blight.chemical: Preventative spray: Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Chlorothalonil 75% WP (@ 2 g/L). Curative spray upon first spot onset: Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Pyraclostrobin 20% WG (@ 1 g/L).
tomato early blight.etl: First appearance of target-board lesions on bottom foliage.
tomato early blight.management: Stake plants and mulch soil. Spray Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (@ 1 ml/L) or Chlorothalonil 75 WP (@ 2 g/L) on bottom leaf spots.

tomato late blight.symptoms: Rapidly expanding water-soaked, irregular pale to dark olive lesions on leaves turning purplish-black and dying within days. Under cool humid conditions (RH >90%, 15-20°C), delicate white cottony downy sporulation develops on lesion margins on lower leaf surface; brown firm leathery rot on green fruit.
tomato late blight.cultural: Avoid sprinkler irrigation; destroy volunteer potato/tomato culls; ensure well-drained raised beds; monitor weather forecast for blight alerts.
tomato late blight.biological: Prophylactic foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum (@ 5g/L) before weather turns foggy.
tomato late blight.chemical: Preventative: Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L). Curative (Emergency): Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (@ 2.5 g/L or 500 g/acre) or Dimethomorph 50% WP (@ 1 g/L) or Metalaxyl-M 4% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Ridomil Gold @ 2.5 g/L).
tomato late blight.etl: Presence of any single late blight lesion under cold humid weather.
tomato late blight.severity: Extreme Emergency (Can wipe out entire field within 72 hours)
tomato late blight.management: Immediately spray Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (@ 2.5 g/L) or Dimethomorph 50 WP (@ 1 g/L) + Mancozeb. Alternate with Ridomil Gold every 7 days.

potato early blight.symptoms: Concentric rings ('target-board' spots) on potato foliage, progressing from lower canopy upward; causes leaf brown blighting and dark sunken corky tuber rot.
potato early blight.cultural: Crop rotation; balanced potash fertilization; avoid water stress.
potato early blight.chemical: Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Azoxystrobin 23% SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Difenoconazole 25% EC (@ 0.5 ml/L).
potato early blight.etl: 1-2 lesions per plant on lower leaves.
potato early blight.management: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) preventatively or Difenoconazole 25 EC (@ 0.5 ml/L) upon spot detection.

potato late blight.symptoms: Water-soaked irregular blackish lesions with white cottony mildew under leaf margins in humid weather; brown dry rot inside harvested tubers.
potato late blight.cultural: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers; earth-up ridges high to protect tubers; dehaulm canopy 10 days before harvest.
potato late blight.biological: Trichoderma harzianum soil and foliar application.
potato late blight.chemical: Spray Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Fenamidone 10% + Mancozeb 50% WG (@ 2.5 g/L) or Mandipropamid 23.4% SC (@ 1 ml/L).
potato late blight.etl: Single lesion found in field or neighborhood blight alert.
potato late blight.severity: Extreme Emergency (Complete Tuber Crop Failure Threat)
potato late blight.management: High earthing-up. Spray Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (@ 2.5 g/L) or Mandipropamid 23.4 SC (@ 1 ml/L) without delay.

tomato bacterial spot.organism: Xanthomonas perforans / Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria
tomato bacterial spot.symptoms: Small (2-3 mm) angular dark greasy water-soaked spots on leaves surrounded by yellow halos, causing shot-holes and ragged defoliation; raised black scab-like pustules on fruit.
tomato bacterial spot.cultural: Use certified pathogen-free seeds; soak seeds in hot water (50°C for 25 min); sanitize nursery trays.
tomato bacterial spot.biological: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens (@ 5g/L) or Bacillus subtilis (@ 5g/L).
tomato bacterial spot.chemical: Foliar spray of Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) tank-mixed with Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm, 1g in 10L water). Repeat at 10-day intervals.
tomato bacterial spot.etl: First appearance of water-soaked spots in nursery or field.
tomato bacterial spot.management: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) combined with Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm). Avoid overhead watering.

tomato yellow virus.organism: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV) - Begomovirus transmitted by Whitefly
tomato yellow virus.symptoms: Severe stunting of young shoots; upward curling and cupping of leaflets; intense interveinal chlorosis (bright golden yellowing); flower abortion and bush-like bushy plant habit.
tomato yellow virus.cultural: Erect 40-mesh insect-proof nylon nets over nurseries; install yellow sticky traps (@ 15/acre); remove and bury infected stunted plants.
tomato yellow virus.biological: Conserve whitefly parasitoids Encarsia formosa; spray Neem oil 1500 ppm (@ 3 ml/L).
tomato yellow virus.chemical: Control whitefly vector: Seedling root dip with Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (@ 0.5 ml/L). Foliar spray of Diafenthiuron 50% WP (@ 1.2 g/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Pyriproxyfen 10% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L).
tomato yellow virus.severity: Critical (Complete Fruit Loss if infected before flowering)
tomato yellow virus.management: Rogue out virus-infected plants immediately. Spray Diafenthiuron 50 WP (@ 1.2 g/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9 SC (@ 1 ml/L) targeting leaf undersides.

tomato septoria spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (1-3 mm) with light grey centers and dark brown borders; tiny black specks (pycnidia) clearly visible inside grey centers.
tomato septoria spot.cultural: Remove lower older leaves; clean stake supports; destroy infected crop debris.
tomato septoria spot.chemical: Spray Chlorothalonil 75% WP (@ 2 g/L) or Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Difenoconazole 25% EC (@ 0.5 ml/L).
tomato septoria spot.etl: 3-5 spots per leaf on lower foliage.
tomato septoria spot.management: Spray Chlorothalonil 75 WP (@ 2 g/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) on bottom canopy.

tomato mold.organism: Passalora fulva (Cladosporium fulvum) - Fungal leaf mold
tomato mold.symptoms: Pale yellow chlorotic patches on upper leaf surface corresponding to velvety olive-green to grayish-brown fungal sporulation patches on lower leaf surface.
tomato mold.cultural: Ventilate polyhouses/greenhouses to reduce relative humidity (<85%); space plants widely; prune bottom suckers.
tomato mold.chemical: Spray Copper Hydroxide 77% WP (@ 2 g/L) or Difenoconazole 25% EC (@ 0.5 ml/L) or Boscalid + Pyraclostrobin.
tomato mold.etl: Initial velvety sporulation on underside of leaves.
tomato mold.management: Improve ventilation in greenhouse. Spray Copper Hydroxide (@ 2 g/L) or Difenoconazole 25 EC (@ 0.5 ml/L).

tomato mosaic virus.symptoms: Mottling with alternating light and dark green areas on leaves; leaflet distortion producing 'shoestring' fern-like foliage; internal browning of fruit wall.
tomato mosaic virus.cultural: Disinfect hands and pruning shears with 20% skimmed milk or 10% trisodium phosphate; prohibit smoking/chewing tobacco in field; rogue infected plants.
tomato mosaic virus.biological: Foliar application of Boerhavia diffusa root extract (10%) to induce systemic acquired resistance.
tomato mosaic virus.chemical: No viricide exists. Apply micronutrient mixture (@ 2 g/L) to sustain plant vigor and reduce mechanical vectoring.
tomato mosaic virus.management: Strict tool sanitation. Rogue out infected plants. Wash hands with milk solution before handling healthy plants.

tomato blight.symptoms: Rapid brown foliar necrosis, branch dieback, and water-soaked leaf blighting.
tomato blight.cultural: Clean sanitation, mulch soil, avoid sprinkler irrigation.
tomato blight.chemical: Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) + Metalaxyl 8% WP (@ 1.5 g/L).
tomato blight.management: Apply Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (@ 2.5 g/L).

chili anthracnose.organism: Colletotrichum capsici / Colletotrichum truncatum - Fungal pathogen
chili anthracnose.symptoms: Small circular dark sunken lesions on ripe red and green fruits with concentric rings of black acervuli ('dieback' phase causes tender twigs to dry from tip downward, turning straw-colored with black spore dots).
chili anthracnose.cultural: Collect and burn dried twigs after harvest; use disease-free seed; maintain balanced potassium fertilization; avoid overhead irrigation.
chili anthracnose.biological: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride (@ 10g/kg); foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens (@ 5g/L) at flowering and fruit set.
chili anthracnose.chemical: Seed treatment with Thiram (@ 3g/kg). Foliar spray of Azoxystrobin 23% SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (@ 1 ml/L or 200 ml/acre) or Propiconazole 25% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L).
chili anthracnose.etl: First appearance of dieback on twigs or 2% fruit infection.
chili anthracnose.severity: Critical (Major Export Rejection Factor in Indian Chili)
chili anthracnose.management: Prune dried twigs. Spray Tebuconazole 25.9 EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Azoxystrobin 23 SC (@ 1 ml/L) at fruit formation stage.

chili curl.organism: Chili Murda / Leaf Curl Complex (Thrips + Yellow Mites + Begomovirus)
chili curl.symptoms: Upward boat-shaped curling of leaves indicates Thrips feeding; downward inverted boat-shaped curling with elongated petioles indicates Yellow Mites; stunted bushy shoots with thickened yellow veins indicates viral infection.
chili curl.cultural: Erect 3 rows of border crops (Maize or Sorghum) to act as windbreak against vector thrips; install blue (for thrips) and yellow (for whiteflies) sticky traps (@ 15 each/acre).
chili curl.biological: Conserve predatory mites (Amblyseius swirskii); spray Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) or Azadirachtin 10,000 ppm (@ 2 ml/L).
chili curl.chemical: For Thrips + Mite complex: Diafenthiuron 50% WP (@ 1.2 g/L) or Fipronil 5% SC (@ 2 ml/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Fenpyroximate 5% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L).
chili curl.management: Install blue and yellow sticky traps. Spray Diafenthiuron 50 WP (@ 1.2 g/L) or Fipronil 5 SC (@ 2 ml/L) targeting leaf surfaces and undersides.

chili curl virus.organism: Chilli Leaf Curl Virus (ChiLCV) - Begomovirus transmitted by Bemisia tabaci
chili curl virus.symptoms: Severe reduction in leaf lamina, thickening and puckering of veins, bushy stunted growth with severe flower drop.
chili curl virus.cultural: Rogue out infected plants immediately; grow nursery under 40-mesh insect-proof netting.
chili curl virus.biological: Spray neem oil 10,000 ppm (@ 2 ml/L); release Encarsia parasitoids.
chili curl virus.chemical: Spray Cyantraniliprole 10.26% OD (@ 1.2 ml/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Flonicamid 50% WG (@ 0.3 g/L).
chili curl virus.management: Erect barrier crops. Control whitefly with Cyantraniliprole 10.26 OD (@ 1.2 ml/L) or Flonicamid 50 WG (@ 0.3 g/L).

chili bacterial spot.symptoms: Dark brown, greasy water-soaked circular lesions on foliage with chlorotic border, causing premature defoliation and blister-like fruit scabs.
chili bacterial spot.cultural: Seed disinfection, hot water treatment, avoid sprinkler irrigation.
chili bacterial spot.chemical: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) + Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm, 1g/10L water).
chili bacterial spot.management: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) with Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm).

chili cercospora spot.symptoms: Large circular spots with distinctive bleached white to grayish centers and dark reddish-brown margins ('frog-eye' spot appearance).
chili cercospora spot.cultural: Maintain good air drainage, collect fallen infected leaves.
chili cercospora spot.chemical: Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Carbendazim 50% WP (@ 1 g/L) or Azoxystrobin 23% SC (@ 1 ml/L).
chili cercospora spot.management: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Carbendazim 50 WP (@ 1 g/L).

chili spot.symptoms: Brown necrotic spots on chili leaves and fruit surfaces.
chili spot.chemical: Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Difenoconazole 25 EC (@ 0.5 ml/L).
chili spot.management: Apply Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Difenoconazole 25 EC (@ 0.5 ml/L).

chili white spot.organism: Cercospora / powdery mildew early bleaching phase
chili white spot.symptoms: Bleached whitish-grey lesions with yellow halos on chili foliage.
chili white spot.cultural: Prune dense lower foliage for air movement.
chili white spot.chemical: Wettable Sulphur 80% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Hexaconazole 5% EC (@ 1 ml/L).
chili white spot.management: Spray Wettable Sulphur 80 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Hexaconazole 5 EC (@ 1 ml/L).

chili nutrition deficiency.organism: Abiotic Physiological Nutrient Deficiency (N, P, K, or Micronutrients Zn/Fe)
chili nutrition deficiency.symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis, pale yellowish foliage, purpling of lower leaf undersides (Phosphorus), or marginal scorching (Potassium).
chili nutrition deficiency.cultural: Conduct soil health card testing; ensure adequate organic matter; correct soil pH.
chili nutrition deficiency.biological: Apply Vesicular Arbuscular Mycorrhiza (VAM @ 10 kg/acre) + Azospirillum bio-fertilizer.
chili nutrition deficiency.chemical: Foliar spray of 19:19:19 NPK soluble fertilizer (@ 5 g/L) + Chelated Zinc EDTA (@ 1 g/L) and Boron (20% @ 1 g/L).
chili nutrition deficiency.management: Apply balanced foliar 19:19:19 NPK spray (@ 5 g/L) enriched with Chelated Zinc EDTA (@ 1 g/L).

bell pepper.organism: Capsicum annuum var. grossum (Bell Pepper foliage)
bell pepper.cultural: Scheduled fertigation, staking, and drip irrigation.
bell pepper.chemical: No intervention required if foliage is clean.

bell pepper spot.organism: Xanthomonas campestris / Cercospora capsici on Capsicum
bell pepper spot.symptoms: Small brown necrotic lesions with chlorotic yellow borders on bell pepper leaves and fruit.
bell pepper spot.cultural: Avoid sprinkler irrigation, ensure drip management.
bell pepper spot.chemical: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) + Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm).
bell pepper spot.management: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) with Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm).

cotton bacterial blight.symptoms: Water-soaked angular leaf spots bounded by veinlets ('angular leaf spot'); brown to dark black lesions extending along veins and girdling main stems and petioles ('blackarm phase'); dark sunken round spots on bolls causing boll rot.
cotton bacterial blight.cultural: Acid delinting of cotton seed with commercial sulfuric acid (100 ml/kg seed); rogue infected plants; avoid high split nitrogen doses.
cotton bacterial blight.biological: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens (@ 10g/kg seed); foliar spray of cow dung filtrate (5%).
cotton bacterial blight.chemical: Seed soaking in Streptocycline solution (100 ppm) for 30 minutes. Foliar spray of Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L or 500 g/acre) plus Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm, 6-8g per 60-80L water) or Plantomycin (@ 1 g/L).
cotton bacterial blight.etl: 5% leaves showing angular spots during squaring stage.
cotton bacterial blight.management: Acid delint seed. Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) tank-mixed with Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm) at initial angular spot onset.

cotton curl virus.organism: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuV) - Begomovirus vectored by Whitefly
cotton curl virus.symptoms: Thickening and darkening of small veins on underside of leaves; upward or downward cup-shaped curling of leaves; enations (leaf-like outgrowths) on lower side of main veins; severe stunting and boll shedding.
cotton curl virus.cultural: Erect barrier crops of pearl millet / sorghum around cotton fields; eradicate volunteer weed hosts like Abutilon indicum (Kanghi) and Xanthium; plant CLCuV-tolerant Bt hybrids.
cotton curl virus.biological: Install yellow sticky traps (@ 20/acre); spray 5% NSKE or Neem oil 1500 ppm (@ 3 ml/L).
cotton curl virus.chemical: Control whitefly vector: Foliar spray of Afidopyropen 50 g/L DC (@ 2 ml/L or 400 ml/acre) or Diafenthiuron 50% WP (@ 1.2 g/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Flonicamid 50% WG (@ 0.4 g/L).
cotton curl virus.management: Destroy weed hosts. Spray Afidopyropen 50 DC (@ 2 ml/L) or Diafenthiuron 50 WP (@ 1.2 g/L) or Flonicamid 50 WG (@ 0.4 g/L) for whitefly control.

wheat yellow rust.organism: Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici - Basidiomycete Stripe Rust
wheat yellow rust.symptoms: Bright yellow to citron-yellow powdery uredinial pustules arranged in linear parallel stripes or rows along the leaf veins; in severe epidemics, heads, glumes, and awns become covered with yellow dust.
wheat yellow rust.cultural: Sow rust-resistant varieties (HD-2967, HD-3086, DBW-187, DBW-303); timely sowing before November 15; avoid over-irrigation during cool foggy spells.
wheat yellow rust.chemical: Foliar spray of Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt @ 1 ml/L or 200 ml in 200 L water/acre) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (@ 1 ml/L). Repeat after 15 days if stripe rust re-emerges.
wheat yellow rust.etl: First notice of yellow pustule stripes on any single plant in field.
wheat yellow rust.severity: Extreme Emergency (Wipes out North Indian Gangetic Plains)
wheat yellow rust.management: Immediately spray Propiconazole 25 EC (@ 1 ml/L, 200 ml/acre) at first appearance of yellow pustule stripes.

wheat brown rust.organism: Puccinia triticina (Puccinia recondita) - Leaf Rust fungus
wheat brown rust.symptoms: Small, round to oval, bright orange-brown powdery pustules scattered randomly (not in stripes) on the upper surface of leaves, shedding brown urediniospores.
wheat brown rust.cultural: Use resistant cultivars; balanced N:P:K fertilization (avoid excess N).
wheat brown rust.chemical: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2 g/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (@ 1 ml/L).
wheat brown rust.etl: 1-2 pustules per leaf on 10% of plants.
wheat brown rust.management: Spray Propiconazole 25 EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9 EC (@ 1 ml/L) at first symptom.

wheat blackrust.organism: Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici - Stem Rust fungus
wheat blackrust.symptoms: Elongated, large reddish-brown to dark chocolate-brown pustules rupturing the epidermis on stems, leaf sheaths, and glumes; pustules produce powdery dark brown spores, later turning black (teliospores).
wheat blackrust.cultural: Grow stem-rust resistant cultivars; avoid late sowing.
wheat blackrust.chemical: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L).
wheat blackrust.etl: Single stem pustule observed in warm climates.
wheat blackrust.severity: Critical (Severe Stem Lodging and Shriveled Grain)
wheat blackrust.management: Apply Propiconazole 25 EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9 EC (@ 1 ml/L).

wheat blast.organism: Magnaporthe oryzae pathotype Triticum - Fungal pathogen
wheat blast.symptoms: Premature bleaching and silvering of wheat spikes/heads while the lower canopy and stem remain green; elliptical grayish-brown lesions on leaves.
wheat blast.cultural: Quarantine surveillance; use certified blast-free seed; avoid seed movement from blast-infected zones.
wheat blast.chemical: Seed treatment with Thiram (@ 3g/kg). Foliar spray of Tebuconazole 25% + Trifloxystrobin 50% WG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Propiconazole 25% EC (@ 1 ml/L) at heading.
wheat blast.management: Foliar spray with Tebuconazole + Trifloxystrobin (@ 0.4 g/L) or Propiconazole 25 EC (@ 1 ml/L) at heading.

wheat mildew.organism: Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici - Powdery Mildew fungus
wheat mildew.symptoms: White to grayish-white powdery or cottony fungal patches on upper surface of leaves and stems, turning yellowish-brown with tiny black cleistothecia as leaves senesce.
wheat mildew.cultural: Avoid dense sowing; avoid excess nitrogen; ensure adequate sun exposure.
wheat mildew.biological: Foliar spray of Ampelomyces quisqualis or Neem oil 1500 ppm (@ 3 ml/L).
wheat mildew.chemical: Foliar spray of Propiconazole 25% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Hexaconazole 5% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Wettable Sulphur 80% WP (@ 2.5 g/L).
wheat mildew.etl: Powdery patches covering 5% of leaf area on lower canopy.
wheat mildew.management: Spray Propiconazole 25 EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Wettable Sulphur 80 WP (@ 2.5 g/L).

wheat septoria.organism: Zymoseptoria tritici / Parastagonospora nodorum - Septoria Leaf Blotch
wheat septoria.symptoms: Irregular brownish-yellow elongated lesions on leaves with conspicuous tiny black specks (pycnidia) embedded inside dead tissue.
wheat septoria.cultural: Crop rotation with non-cereal crops; deep burial of wheat straw.
wheat septoria.chemical: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Azoxystrobin 23% SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Chlorothalonil 75% WP (@ 2 g/L).
wheat septoria.etl: 5% leaf area affected on lower foliage.
wheat septoria.management: Spray Propiconazole 25 EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Chlorothalonil 75 WP (@ 2 g/L).

wheat blight.organism: Bipolaris sorokiniana - Spot Blotch / Foliar Blight
wheat blight.symptoms: Small brown oval spots enlarging into dark brown necrotic blotches with yellow margins on leaves under warm humid post-anthesis conditions.
wheat blight.cultural: Seed treatment; zero-tillage sowing; balanced fertilization with potash.
wheat blight.chemical: Propiconazole 25% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L).
wheat blight.etl: Spot blotch lesions on flag leaf and penultimate leaf.
wheat blight.management: Apply Propiconazole 25 EC (@ 1 ml/L) at boot leaf to heading stage.

wheat commonrootrot.organism: Bipolaris sorokiniana / Fusarium spp. - Root Rot Complex
wheat commonrootrot.symptoms: Dark brown to black necrotic lesions on subcrown internode and crown roots; premature ripening of tillers resulting in whiteheads with shriveled grain.
wheat commonrootrot.cultural: Crop rotation with legumes; avoid deep planting; balanced fertilization.
wheat commonrootrot.chemical: Seed treatment with Carboxin 37.5% + Thiram 37.5% WS (@ 2.5 g/kg seed).
wheat commonrootrot.management: Seed treatment with Carboxin + Thiram (@ 2.5 g/kg) and avoid planting too deeply.

wheat fusariumheadblight.symptoms: Bleaching of individual spikelets or entire heads while stem is green; pinkish-orange fungal spore masses at glume margins; grain chalky, shriveled (tombstones) contaminated with deoxynivalenol (DON) mycotoxin.
wheat fusariumheadblight.cultural: Avoid wheat following corn in crop rotation; destroy crop residue; monitor rainfall during anthesis.
wheat fusariumheadblight.biological: Bacillus subtilis foliar spray at early flowering.
wheat fusariumheadblight.chemical: Spray Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Metconazole or Propiconazole (@ 1 ml/L) precisely during early flowering (50% anthesis).
wheat fusariumheadblight.etl: First bleached spikelet during wet anthesis.
wheat fusariumheadblight.management: Spray Tebuconazole 25.9 EC (@ 1 ml/L) strictly at 50% anthesis to protect emerging heads.

wheat smut.symptoms: Every spikelet of the wheat ear is transformed into a loose, powdery mass of dark olive-black smut spores; delicate membrane ruptures early, leaving only the bare naked rachis.
wheat smut.cultural: Solar heat seed treatment (soak seeds in water for 4 hrs, then spread in blazing June sun for 4 hrs); use certified disease-free seed.
wheat smut.chemical: Mandatory seed treatment with Carboxin 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/kg) or Tebuconazole 2% DS (@ 1.5 g/kg seed).
wheat smut.management: Solar seed treatment in summer or chemical seed dressing with Carboxin (@ 2.5 g/kg) or Tebuconazole.

wheat tanspot.symptoms: Small tan to brown spots with distinctive tiny yellow chlorotic halos, coalescing into extensive necrotic foliar blighting.
wheat tanspot.cultural: Bury stubbles; rotate with broadleaf non-host crops.
wheat tanspot.chemical: Propiconazole 25% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Azoxystrobin 23% SC (@ 1 ml/L).
wheat tanspot.management: Spray Propiconazole 25 EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Azoxystrobin 23 SC (@ 1 ml/L).

wheat aphid.organism: Sitobion avenae / Rhopalosiphum padi (Wheat Aphid / Oat Bird-cherry Aphid)
wheat aphid.symptoms: Dense colonies of green aphids clustering on tender leaves, shoots, and inside emerging ears/panicles, sucking phloem sap causing grain shriveling; copious honeydew.
wheat aphid.cultural: Balanced nitrogen application; conserve predatory ladybird beetles.
wheat aphid.biological: Conserve Coccinella septempunctata (ladybird beetles @ 1 beetle/plant) and Chrysoperla carnea; spray Neem oil 1500 ppm (@ 3 ml/L).
wheat aphid.chemical: Spray Thiamethoxam 25% WG (@ 0.25 g/L or 50 g/acre) or Dimethoate 30% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L) or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (@ 0.3 ml/L).
wheat aphid.etl: 5-10 aphids per ear/shoot during earhead stage.
wheat aphid.management: Conserve ladybird beetles. Spray Thiamethoxam 25 WG (@ 0.25 g/L) or Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (@ 0.3 ml/L).

wheat mite.symptoms: Foliage develops mottled yellow and silvery speckles, drying up from tip downward giving field a scorched or frosted appearance during dry spells.
wheat mite.cultural: Provide immediate light irrigation to wash mites off canopy; deep plowing.
wheat mite.biological: Conserve predatory mites; spray Wettable Sulphur 80% WP (@ 2.5 g/L).
wheat mite.chemical: Spray Propargite 57% EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Dimethoate 30% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L).
wheat mite.management: Apply immediate irrigation. Spray Wettable Sulphur 80 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Propargite 57 EC (@ 2 ml/L).

wheat sawfly.symptoms: Larvae tunnel inside wheat stem internodes, hollowing stem and girdling interior base, causing lodging of mature stems right before harvest.
wheat sawfly.cultural: Plant solid-stemmed wheat varieties; deep fall tillage to expose overwintering cocoons; swathing lodged grain.
wheat sawfly.chemical: Foliar insecticides have limited efficacy due to internal tunneling; border spray with Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 2 ml/L) during adult flight.
wheat sawfly.management: Plant solid-stemmed cultivars and deep plow stubble after harvest.

wheat blossom midge.organism: Sitodiplosis mosellana - Orange Wheat Blossom Midge
wheat blossom midge.symptoms: Orange maggots feed directly on developing wheat kernels inside glumes, causing stunted, deformed, and shriveled kernels.
wheat blossom midge.cultural: Sow resistant cultivars; rotate with non-susceptible crops.
wheat blossom midge.chemical: Spray Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Lambdacyhalothrin 5% EC (@ 0.5 ml/L) at dusk during adult flight at heading.
wheat blossom midge.etl: 1 adult midge per 4-5 wheat heads at heading.
wheat blossom midge.management: Apply Lambdacyhalothrin 5 EC (@ 0.5 ml/L) at dusk during heading.

groundnut early spot.organism: Cercospora arachidicola - Early Tikka Leaf Spot
groundnut early spot.symptoms: Circular reddish-brown to dark brown spots (1-10 mm) on upper leaf surface, surrounded by a prominent bright yellow chlorotic halo. Causes heavy premature defoliation.
groundnut early spot.cultural: Crop rotation with cereals (sorghum, pearl millet); deep plowing of crop residues; timely sowing.
groundnut early spot.biological: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride 1% WP (@ 10g/kg); foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens (@ 5g/L).
groundnut early spot.chemical: Foliar spray of Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP (Saaf @ 2 g/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Chlorothalonil 75% WP (@ 2 g/L) or Hexaconazole 5% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L).
groundnut early spot.etl: First spotting observed on lower leaves at 30-40 days after sowing.
groundnut early spot.management: Spray Carbendazim + Mancozeb (Saaf @ 2 g/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9 EC (@ 1 ml/L) at first spot appearance.

groundnut late spot.organism: Phaeoisariopsis personata (Cercosporidium personatum) - Late Tikka Spot
groundnut late spot.symptoms: Nearly circular, smaller, darker black spots without yellow halos or with faint diffuse halo, with abundant carbon-black cushion-like conidial fruiting bodies on lower leaf surface.
groundnut late spot.cultural: Destroy crop residues; avoid continuous groundnut mono-cropping; balanced potassium application.
groundnut late spot.biological: Spray NSKE 5% or Trichoderma viride foliar suspension.
groundnut late spot.chemical: Spray Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Difenoconazole 25% EC (@ 0.5 ml/L).
groundnut late spot.etl: 5% leaf area affected on lower foliage.
groundnut late spot.management: Spray Tebuconazole 25.9 EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Hexaconazole 5 EC (@ 1.5 ml/L) targeting lower leaf surface.

groundnut rust.symptoms: Numerous small, circular, orange-brown pustules on lower leaf surface, rupturing to expose reddish-brown powdery urediniospores; leaves curl, become necrotic, and dry like parchment paper.
groundnut rust.cultural: Sow resistant varieties; practice crop rotation; remove volunteer groundnut plants.
groundnut rust.biological: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens (@ 5g/L) or Verticillium lecanii.
groundnut rust.chemical: Spray Hexaconazole 5% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L) or Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Wettable Sulphur 80% WP (@ 2.5 g/L).
groundnut rust.etl: 1-2 rust pustules per leaflet on lower canopy.
groundnut rust.management: Spray Hexaconazole 5 EC (@ 1.5 ml/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9 EC (@ 1 ml/L) at first pustule detection.

groundnut early rust.symptoms: Orange-yellow pinhead pustules on leaf undersides progressing to brown powder.
groundnut early rust.chemical: Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Hexaconazole 5 EC (@ 1.5 ml/L).
groundnut early rust.management: Apply Hexaconazole 5 EC (@ 1.5 ml/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L).

groundnut nutrition deficiency.organism: Abiotic Deficiency (Iron Chlorosis / Zinc / Calcium deficiency)
groundnut nutrition deficiency.symptoms: Interveinal yellowing of young leaves turning bleached ivory-white (Iron chlorosis on calcareous soils); poor pod filling / empty pods ('pops' due to Calcium deficiency).
groundnut nutrition deficiency.cultural: Apply Gypsum (@ 200 kg/acre) at 40-45 days after sowing (flowering/pegging) to supply calcium and sulfur.
groundnut nutrition deficiency.biological: Soil application of VAM mycorrhiza and PSB bio-fertilizers.
groundnut nutrition deficiency.chemical: For iron chlorosis: Foliar spray of Ferrous Sulphate (FeSO4 @ 5 g/L) + Citric acid (@ 1 g/L). For zinc: Zinc Sulphate (@ 2 g/L).
groundnut nutrition deficiency.etl: Yellowing of terminal leaves across rows.
groundnut nutrition deficiency.management: Apply Gypsum (@ 200 kg/acre) at pegging. Foliar spray Ferrous Sulphate (5 g/L) + Citric acid (1 g/L) for chlorosis.

citrus canker.organism: Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri - Bacterial Pathogen
citrus canker.symptoms: Small, raised, blister-like corky tan-to-brown craterous lesions with rough erupted surfaces surrounded by a distinct oily or water-soaked yellow halo; lesions occur on leaves, twigs, thorns, and fruit rind causing severe fruit drop.
citrus canker.cultural: Prune severely cankered twigs before monsoon rains and burn them; establish windbreaks (Sesbania / Casuarina) to prevent wind-driven rain splashes.
citrus canker.biological: Foliar spray of neem cake extract (5%) or Pseudomonas fluorescens (@ 5g/L).
citrus canker.chemical: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L or 250 g in 100 L water) mixed with Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm, 10g in 100 L water). Apply at flush initiation and repeat after fruit set.
citrus canker.etl: First appearance of raised corky spots on young flush leaves.
citrus canker.severity: Critical (Severe Export Rejection & Canker Fruit Drop)
citrus canker.management: Prune cankered twigs. Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) combined with Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm) during new leaf flush.

citrus black spot.symptoms: Hard round black spots with depressed grey centers and dark reddish-brown elevated borders on fruit rind and leaves; causes premature fruit drop and unsightly rinds.
citrus black spot.cultural: Remove fallen diseased citrus leaves from orchard floor; maintain tree canopy aeration through balanced pruning.
citrus black spot.chemical: Foliar spray of Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Azoxystrobin 23% SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) at petal fall and repeat at 4-week intervals.
citrus black spot.etl: Presence of black spots on mature fruit or young foliage.
citrus black spot.management: Clear orchard floor debris. Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Azoxystrobin 23 SC (@ 1 ml/L) starting at petal fall.

phyllocnistis citrella stainton.symptoms: Tiny larvae mine inside young tender leaf cuticles, creating serpentine silvery translucent zigzag galleries; leaves curl, distort, and provide major entry wounds for Citrus Canker bacteria.
phyllocnistis citrella stainton.cultural: Synchronize flush by balanced pruning; avoid staggered flushes; prune off water sprouts/suckers.
phyllocnistis citrella stainton.biological: Conserve eulophid parasitoids (Cirrospilus ingenuus); spray 5% NSKE or Neem oil 1500 ppm (@ 3 ml/L).
phyllocnistis citrella stainton.chemical: Foliar spray during active flush emergence: Thiamethoxam 25% WG (@ 0.3 g/L) or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (@ 0.5 ml/L) or Spinosad 45% SC (@ 0.3 ml/L).
phyllocnistis citrella stainton.etl: 5% of young tender flush leaves mined.
phyllocnistis citrella stainton.management: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (@ 0.5 ml/L) or Thiamethoxam 25 WG (@ 0.3 g/L) during emergence of new leaf flush.

panonchus citri mcgregor.symptoms: Mites suck chlorophyll from upper leaf surfaces, producing pale stippling or scratching that coalesces into a dull gray/bronze foliage; heavy attacks cause twig dieback and fruit dropping.
panonchus citri mcgregor.cultural: Maintain adequate tree irrigation; preserve natural predatory phytoseiid mites.
panonchus citri mcgregor.biological: Spray Wettable Sulphur 80% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or horticultural mineral oil (1-2%).
panonchus citri mcgregor.chemical: Spray Propargite 57% EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Fenazaquin 10% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L).
panonchus citri mcgregor.management: Spray Wettable Sulphur 80 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9 SC (@ 1 ml/L) on both leaf surfaces.

toxoptera citricidus.symptoms: Dense black/brown aphid colonies curling young tender shoot tips, secreting copious honeydew leading to thick sooty mold; primary vector of Citrus Tristeza Virus (CTV).
toxoptera citricidus.cultural: Prune water shoots; avoid excessive nitrogen.
toxoptera citricidus.biological: Conserve ladybird beetles and syrphid fly larvae; spray Neem oil (@ 3 ml/L).
toxoptera citricidus.chemical: Foliar spray of Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Thiamethoxam 25% WG (@ 0.25 g/L) or Acetamiprid 20% SP (@ 0.2 g/L).
toxoptera citricidus.management: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Thiamethoxam 25 WG (@ 0.25 g/L) on new shoots.

toxoptera aurantii.symptoms: Colonies cluster on young flushes and buds; leaf cupping, curling, and sooty mold.
toxoptera aurantii.chemical: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Dimethoate 30% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L).
toxoptera aurantii.management: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Dimethoate 30 EC (@ 1.5 ml/L).

banana sigatoka.organism: Pseudocercospora musae / P. fijiensis (Yellow & Black Sigatoka)
banana sigatoka.symptoms: Small yellowish-green streaks running parallel to leaf veins, developing into dark reddish-brown elliptical spots with sunken bleached grayish centers and yellow halos, coalescing to destroy the photosynthetic canopy.
banana sigatoka.cultural: De-leafing (cut off and burn infected leaves or bury them leaf-surface down); maintain proper plantation drainage; keep spacing 1.8x1.8 m.
banana sigatoka.biological: Pseudomonas fluorescens (@ 5g/L) foliar spray mixed with 1% agricultural mineral oil.
banana sigatoka.chemical: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Carbendazim 50% WP (@ 1 g/L) or Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) emulsified with 1% mineral spray oil (Banana spray oil).
banana sigatoka.etl: First spotting visible on 3rd or 4th youngest open leaf.
banana sigatoka.management: Prompt de-leafing of necrotic foliage. Spray Propiconazole 25 EC (@ 1 ml/L) mixed with 1% mineral spray oil.

banana panama.organism: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense (Race 1 / Tropical Race 4 - TR4)
banana panama.symptoms: Yellowing of lower older leaves starting from leaf margins and progressing to petiole, forming a protective skirt of dead leaves hanging around pseudostem; longitudinal splitting of pseudostem base; reddish-brown vascular discoloration inside corm.
banana panama.cultural: Strict farm biosecurity; plant tissue culture plants certified TR4-free; avoid waterlogging; apply bio-primed farmyard manure.
banana panama.biological: Apply Trichoderma viride / reesei (ICAR-FUSICONT formulation @ 2.5 kg/plant enriched in FYM) into planting pits.
banana panama.chemical: Soil drenching around pseudostem with Carbendazim 50% WP (@ 2 g/L) or inject pseudostem with 2% Carbendazim solution.
banana panama.etl: Single symptomatic plant detected in plantation.
banana panama.management: Isolate infected mats. Apply Trichoderma-enriched FYM (ICAR-FUSICONT). Drench soil with Carbendazim 50 WP (@ 2 g/L).

banana cordana.symptoms: Large oval to diamond-shaped pale brown necrotic spots with prominent bright yellow zigzag borders, typically starting from leaf margins and expanding inward.
banana cordana.cultural: Remove and destroy dried necrotic leaves; avoid water stagnation in root zone.
banana cordana.chemical: Foliar spray of Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2 g/L) or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) at early symptom onset.
banana cordana.management: Prune severely affected leaf margins. Spray Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2 g/L) or Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L).

banana moko.symptoms: Pale green/yellow wilting of inner younger leaves; pseudostem vascular bundles show dark brown/black discoloration; white bacterial ooze exudes when infected vascular strands are immersed in clear water.
banana moko.cultural: Strict domestic quarantine; eradicate infected mats immediately by injecting glyphosate or burning in situ; sanitize machetes with 10% bleach.
banana moko.biological: Soil application of antagonistic Bacillus subtilis.
banana moko.chemical: Soil disinfection with bleaching powder (30 kg/ha); no curative chemical therapy once systemic.
banana moko.management: Immediate eradication of infected plant mat with herbicide. Disinfect cutting tools with 10% sodium hypochlorite.

banana bract mosaic virus.organism: Banana Bract Mosaic Virus (BBrMV) - Potyvirus vectored by Aphids
banana bract mosaic virus.symptoms: Spindle-shaped reddish-brown to dark purple streaks on leaf petioles, pseudostem, and flower bracts; bunches fail to emerge properly or are choked.
banana bract mosaic virus.cultural: Use certified virus-indexed tissue culture plantlets; rogue infected stools immediately.
banana bract mosaic virus.biological: Conserve aphid predators; spray neem extract.
banana bract mosaic virus.chemical: Control aphid vector (Pentalonia nigronervosa): Spray Dimethoate 30% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L) or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (@ 0.3 ml/L).
banana bract mosaic virus.etl: Presence of mosaic symptoms on bracts or leaf sheaths.
banana bract mosaic virus.management: Rogue out infected plants. Spray Dimethoate 30 EC (@ 1.5 ml/L) or Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (@ 0.3 ml/L) for aphid vector.

banana insectpest.organism: Odoiporus longicollis (Banana Pseudostem Weevil / Rhizome Weevil)
banana insectpest.symptoms: Small pinhead feeding punctures on pseudostem oozing transparent jelly-like sap; grubs bore inside pseudostem making honeycombed galleries, causing stem breakage during bunch filling.
banana insectpest.cultural: Field sanitation; use longitudinal split pseudostem traps (@ 25-50 traps/acre) to collect and destroy adult weevils manually.
banana insectpest.biological: Apply entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana (@ 5g/L or swab trunk); entomopathogenic nematodes (Heterorhabditis).
banana insectpest.chemical: Trunk injection or stem swabbing: Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 2.5 ml/L) or Carbofuran 3G (@ 20g/plant applied in leaf axils).
banana insectpest.management: Place split pseudostem traps (25/acre). Swab trunk with Chlorpyrifos 20 EC (@ 2.5 ml/L) or Beauveria bassiana (@ 5g/L).

banana pestalotiopsis.organism: Pestalotiopsis palmarum - Secondary Fungal Leaf Spot
banana pestalotiopsis.symptoms: Ash-grey oval to irregular lesions with dark margins on weakened or sunburnt banana leaves.
banana pestalotiopsis.chemical: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2 g/L).
banana pestalotiopsis.management: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2 g/L).

corn northern blight.organism: Exserohilum turcicum (Setosphaeria turcica) - Turcicum Leaf Blight
corn northern blight.symptoms: Large, elongated, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2.5 to 15 cm long) with smooth margins on leaf blades; under moist conditions, olive-green fungal sporulation covers lesion surfaces.
corn northern blight.cultural: Crop rotation with non-graminaceous crops; deep plowing of crop residues; plant tolerant corn hybrids.
corn northern blight.biological: Trichoderma viride seed and foliar spray.
corn northern blight.chemical: Foliar spray of Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC (@ 1 ml/L or 200 ml/acre) or Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) at tasseling/silking.
corn northern blight.etl: 1-2 cigar lesions per leaf at tasseling.
corn northern blight.management: Spray Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (@ 1 ml/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) upon appearance of cigar-shaped lesions.

corn blight.organism: Exserohilum turcicum / Bipolaris maydis - Foliar Blight Complex
corn blight.symptoms: Elongated tan lesions on maize leaf blades progressing into complete foliar blighting.
corn blight.chemical: Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Azoxystrobin 23% SC (@ 1 ml/L).
corn blight.etl: Early lesion onset on mid-canopy leaves.
corn blight.management: Apply Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Azoxystrobin 23 SC (@ 1 ml/L).

corn southern blight.organism: Bipolaris maydis (Cochliobolus heterostrophus) - Maydis Leaf Blight
corn southern blight.symptoms: Small, oval, spindle-shaped light brown lesions with purplish margins, bounded by leaf veins; smaller and more numerous than northern blight.
corn southern blight.cultural: Rotate with legumes, plant resistant varieties.
corn southern blight.chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Propiconazole 25% EC (@ 1 ml/L).
corn southern blight.management: Spray Propiconazole 25 EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L).

corn gray spot.symptoms: Distinctly rectangular, narrow tan-to-gray lesions strictly delineated by leaf veins ('stripes' or 'ribbons' parallel to veins).
corn gray spot.cultural: Crop rotation, reduce residue on soil surface, choose resistant hybrids.
corn gray spot.chemical: Spray Pyraclostrobin 20% WG (@ 1 g/L) or Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (@ 1 ml/L).
corn gray spot.etl: Lesions on third leaf below ear leaf at silking.
corn gray spot.management: Spray Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (@ 1 ml/L) or Pyraclostrobin 20 WG (@ 1 g/L).

corn rust.symptoms: Small, powdery, oval to elongate golden-brown to cinnamon-brown pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
corn rust.chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Propiconazole 25% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Hexaconazole 5% EC (@ 1 ml/L).
corn rust.management: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Propiconazole 25 EC (@ 1 ml/L).

corn borer.organism: Chilo partellus (Spotted Stem Borer) / Spodoptera frugiperda (Fall Armyworm)
corn borer.symptoms: Parallel pinhole 'shot-holes' on expanding leaves; extensive frass (sawdust-like excreta) inside central leaf whorl; tassel breakage and ear boring.
corn borer.cultural: Intercrop with cowpea or desmodium; deploy pheromone traps (@ 5/acre); whorl application of sand + lime mixture (9:1).
corn borer.biological: Release Trichogramma chilonis (@ 1.5 lakh/ha); apply Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt @ 2 g/L) or Metarhizium anisopliae into whorls.
corn borer.chemical: Whorl application of Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (@ 0.4 ml/L) or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG (@ 0.4 g/L or 80 g/acre) or Spinetoram 11.7% SC (@ 0.5 ml/L).
corn borer.etl: 5% infested whorls in seedling stage, 10% in mid-whorl stage.
corn borer.management: Whorl drop application of Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (@ 0.4 ml/L).

fall armyworm.symptoms: Large ragged feeding holes, skeletonized leaves, heavy accumulating moist sawdust-like fecal frass in central whorls; inverted 'Y' suture on head.
fall armyworm.cultural: Deep summer plowing; handpick egg masses; whorl application of sand or wood ash.
fall armyworm.biological: Release egg parasitoids Trichogramma pretiosum (@ 50,000/acre); spray Nomuraea rileyi or Metarhizium rileyi (@ 5g/L).
fall armyworm.chemical: Spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (@ 0.4 ml/L) or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Spinetoram 11.7% SC (@ 0.5 ml/L) directing spray into whorls.
fall armyworm.etl: 5% damaged whorls in early stage; 10% in mid-whorl.
fall armyworm.management: Direct spray into central leaf whorl: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (@ 0.4 ml/L) or Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG (@ 0.4 g/L).

faw symptoms.symptoms: Windowpane feeding on leaf lamina, chewed whorl leaves, frass clumping.
faw symptoms.chemical: Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (@ 0.4 ml/L).
faw symptoms.management: Whorl application of Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG (@ 0.4 g/L).

maize spot.organism: Bipolaris / Cercospora foliar spots on Maize
maize spot.symptoms: Chlorotic to necrotic spotting across maize leaf lamina.
maize spot.chemical: Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Azoxystrobin 23 SC (@ 1 ml/L).

maize streak virus.organism: Maize Streak Virus (MSV) - Mastrevirus transmitted by Leafhopper Cicadulina mbila
maize streak virus.symptoms: Very small circular chlorotic spots on young leaves developing into continuous uniform narrow yellowish-white chlorotic stripes parallel to leaf veins.
maize streak virus.cultural: Control volunteer grasses; rogue early infected plants; plant streak-resistant maize hybrids.
maize streak virus.chemical: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid 70% WS (@ 4 g/kg seed) to control leafhopper vector; spray Thiamethoxam 25% WG (@ 0.3 g/L).
maize streak virus.management: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid 70 WS. Spray Thiamethoxam 25 WG (@ 0.3 g/L) for vector leafhopper control.

sugarcane brown spot.symptoms: Reddish-brown narrow oval spots with yellow halo on both leaf surfaces, coalescing into large necrotic blights.
sugarcane brown spot.cultural: Ensure field drainage; burn trash after harvest in heavily infested fields.
sugarcane brown spot.chemical: Foliar spray of Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Carbendazim 50% WP (@ 1 g/L).
sugarcane brown spot.management: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Carbendazim 50 WP (@ 1 g/L).

sugarcane grassy shoot.organism: Sugarcane Grassy Shoot Phytoplasma (GSD) transmitted by Aphids / Leafhoppers
sugarcane grassy shoot.symptoms: Proliferation of dense, thin, narrow chlorotic tillers from the base of the stool giving it a broom-like or grassy tuft appearance ('grassy shoot'); leaves turn completely bleached yellowish-white without cane formation.
sugarcane grassy shoot.cultural: Hot Water Treatment (HWT) of seed cane setts at 50°C for 2 hours or Aerated Steam Therapy (AST) at 54°C for 1 hour; rogue infected grassy stools.
sugarcane grassy shoot.chemical: Control insect vectors: Spray Dimethoate 30% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L) or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (@ 0.3 ml/L).
sugarcane grassy shoot.severity: Critical (Zero Cane Yield from Grassy Stools)
sugarcane grassy shoot.management: Hot water treat setts before planting. Rogue out grassy stools. Spray Dimethoate 30 EC (@ 1.5 ml/L) for vector control.

apple scab.symptoms: Velvety olive-green to dull dark brown circular spots with indistinct margins on leaves; spots turn dark brown, corky, and scabbed; on fruit, lesions become dark, sunken, corky with cracked fissures.
apple scab.cultural: Post-harvest orchard sanitation: spray 5% urea on fallen leaves in autumn to accelerate leaf decomposition and eliminate overwintering pseudothecia.
apple scab.biological: Prophylactic application of Bacillus subtilis or Trichoderma viride.
apple scab.chemical: Silver tip to green tip stage: Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Captan 50% WP (@ 2 g/L). Petal fall / fruit development: Difenoconazole 25% EC (@ 0.5 ml/L) or Hexaconazole 5% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Kresoxim-methyl 44.3% SC (@ 0.5 ml/L).
apple scab.etl: Mills Infection Period criteria met (leaf wetness hours vs temperature).
apple scab.severity: Critical (Primary Export Quality Rejection in Apple)
apple scab.management: Autumn 5% urea spray on fallen litter. Spray Difenoconazole 25 EC (@ 0.5 ml/L) or Kresoxim-methyl 44.3 SC (@ 0.5 ml/L) from petal fall.

apple rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange circular spots on upper leaf surface, exuding sweet drops; later, raised orange cushions develop tiny tube-like cluster cups (aecia) on lower leaf surface.
apple rust.cultural: Eradicate alternate host red cedar (Juniperus virginiana) within 1-2 km radius of apple orchards.
apple rust.chemical: Spray Myclobutanil 10% WP (@ 0.5 g/L) or Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (@ 1 ml/L) at pink bud through petal fall.
apple rust.management: Remove nearby cedar alternate hosts. Spray Myclobutanil 10 WP (@ 0.5 g/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) from pink bud stage.

grape black rot.symptoms: Circular reddish-brown leaf spots with dark margins and tiny black pycnidia; infected berries turn purple-brown, shrivel, and dry into hard, wrinkled black mummies that remain attached to bunch.
grape black rot.cultural: Prune out mummified berries and infected canes during dormancy; ensure good canopy sunlight penetration.
grape black rot.biological: Trichoderma spray on pruned vine cuts.
grape black rot.chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Difenoconazole 25% EC (@ 0.5 ml/L) or Azoxystrobin 23% SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Myclobutanil 10% WP (@ 0.5 g/L) before bloom and at pea-sized berry stage.
grape black rot.etl: Single leaf lesion or mummified berry.
grape black rot.management: Destroy mummified berry clusters. Spray Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Difenoconazole 25 EC (@ 0.5 ml/L) before flowering and after fruit set.

colomerus vitis.organism: Colomerus vitis - Grape Leaf Blister Mite / Erineum Mite
colomerus vitis.symptoms: Upper leaf surface forms prominent convex blisters or galls; corresponding lower leaf cavities are filled with dense, felt-like, whitish to yellowish-brown erinea (hairs).
colomerus vitis.cultural: Prune heavily blistered canes in winter; destroy pruned material.
colomerus vitis.biological: Conserve predatory phytoseiid mites; spray Wettable Sulphur 80% WP (@ 2.5 g/L).
colomerus vitis.chemical: Spray Wettable Sulphur 80% WP (@ 2.5 g/L or 2.5 kg/ha) or Propargite 57% EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (@ 1 ml/L).
colomerus vitis.management: Spray Wettable Sulphur 80 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9 SC (@ 1 ml/L) during early shoot growth.

viteus vitifoliae.symptoms: Yellowish galls on leaf undersides; nodule-like galls on young roots (nodosities) and hook-like necrotic swellings on older roots (tuberosities) causing vine death.
viteus vitifoliae.cultural: Graft commercial scions onto phylloxera-resistant rootstocks (e.g. 110R, 1103P, SO4); flood vineyard where feasible.
viteus vitifoliae.chemical: Soil drenching with Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (@ 0.5 ml/L); resistant rootstocks are the only permanent control.
viteus vitifoliae.management: Use certified phylloxera-resistant rootstocks. Soil drench with Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (@ 0.5 ml/L).

cauliflower blackrot.symptoms: V-shaped chlorotic to yellow lesions emerging from leaf margins with base of 'V' pointing inward toward leaf veins; leaf veins turn distinctly black or dark brown; vascular browning in curds and stems.
cauliflower blackrot.cultural: Hot water seed treatment (50°C for 30 minutes); 3-year crop rotation without cruciferous crops; rogue infected plants.
cauliflower blackrot.chemical: Foliar spray of Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) mixed with Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm, 1g/10L water). Repeat at 10-day intervals.
cauliflower blackrot.etl: First margin V-shaped yellowing noticed in nursery or field.
cauliflower blackrot.management: Hot water seed treatment (50°C for 30 min). Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) with Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm).

cauliflower bacterial spot rot.organism: Pseudomonas syringae pv. maculicola / Pectobacterium carotovorum
cauliflower bacterial spot rot.symptoms: Small water-soaked translucent spots on leaves and soft slimy brown wet rot on cauliflower curds with foul odor.
cauliflower bacterial spot rot.cultural: Avoid curd injury during weeding; harvest curds during dry hours; avoid sprinkler irrigation.
cauliflower bacterial spot rot.chemical: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) + Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm).
cauliflower bacterial spot rot.management: Avoid waterlogging. Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) with Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm).

cauliflower downy mildew.symptoms: Angular purplish-brown to yellow lesions on upper leaf surface corresponding to white fluffy downy mildew growth on lower leaf surface; curd internal browning.
cauliflower downy mildew.cultural: Proper nursery drainage; avoid dense sowing; rotate with solanaceous crops.
cauliflower downy mildew.chemical: Spray Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Ridomil Gold @ 2.5 g/L) or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Dimethomorph 50% WP (@ 1 g/L).
cauliflower downy mildew.etl: White downy growth on 5% of nursery seedlings.
cauliflower downy mildew.management: Spray Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold @ 2.5 g/L) or Dimethomorph 50 WP (@ 1 g/L).

radish black spot.organism: Alternaria brassicae / A. brassicicola - Fungal Leaf Spot
radish black spot.symptoms: Dark brown to black circular zonate spots with concentric rings on radish leaves, siliquae, and exposed roots.
radish black spot.cultural: Clean certified seeds, burn infected radish tops.
radish black spot.chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Iprodione 50% WP (@ 2 g/L).
radish black spot.management: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Iprodione 50 WP (@ 2 g/L).

radish downey mildew.symptoms: Yellow angular patches on upper leaf surface with white downy fungal growth on lower surface.
radish downey mildew.chemical: Ridomil Gold (@ 2.5 g/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L).
radish downey mildew.management: Spray Ridomil Gold (@ 2.5 g/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L).

radish mosaic.organism: Radish Mosaic Virus (RaMV) transmitted by Flea Beetles
radish mosaic.symptoms: Interspersed light green and dark green mosaic patterns, blistering, and leaf distortion.
radish mosaic.cultural: Rogue out infected plants; clean weeds.
radish mosaic.chemical: Control flea beetle vectors: Spray Cypermethrin 10% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (@ 0.3 ml/L).
radish mosaic.management: Control vector flea beetles with Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (@ 0.3 ml/L).

radish flea beetle.symptoms: Adult beetles chew numerous small round 'shot-holes' in cotyledons and tender leaves.
radish flea beetle.cultural: Install yellow sticky traps; cover beds with floating row covers.
radish flea beetle.biological: Spray Beauveria bassiana (@ 5g/L) or Neem oil 1500 ppm (@ 3 ml/L).
radish flea beetle.chemical: Spray Thiamethoxam 25% WG (@ 0.3 g/L) or Cypermethrin 10% EC (@ 1 ml/L).
radish flea beetle.management: Spray Thiamethoxam 25 WG (@ 0.3 g/L) or Cypermethrin 10 EC (@ 1 ml/L).

papaya ringspot.organism: Papaya Ringspot Virus (PRSV) - Potyvirus vectored by Aphids
papaya ringspot.symptoms: Severe foliar yellow mosaic and blistered deformation with leaf lamina reduction ('shoestring' appearance); dark green oily water-soaked streaks on petioles; conspicuous dark green concentric rings on fruit skin.
papaya ringspot.cultural: Isolate papaya orchards from cucurbits (alternate aphid hosts); rogue and burn virus-infected trees immediately; grow border barrier of maize or sorghum.
papaya ringspot.biological: Spray NSKE 5% or Neem oil 10,000 ppm (@ 2 ml/L).
papaya ringspot.chemical: No chemical cures the virus. Control aphid vectors with Dimethoate 30% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L) or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (@ 0.3 ml/L); apply zinc and boron micronutrients.
papaya ringspot.management: Eradicate infected trees. Plant border barrier of maize. Spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (@ 0.3 ml/L) for aphid control.

papaya bacterialspot.symptoms: Angular water-soaked leaf spots turning brown and causing blighting; petiole cankers.
papaya bacterialspot.chemical: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) + Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm).
papaya bacterialspot.management: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) with Streptocycline (@ 100 ppm).

cashew red rust.symptoms: Circular, velvety, reddish-brown to rust-colored raised algal spots on upper leaf surfaces and green twigs.
cashew red rust.cultural: Prune overcrowded overlapping branches to enhance sunlight penetration; improve orchard drainage.
cashew red rust.chemical: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Bordeaux mixture (1%) before new flush.
cashew red rust.etl: Algal spots on 10% of flush foliage.
cashew red rust.management: Prune dense canopies for sunlight. Spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or 1% Bordeaux mixture.

cassava mosaic.organism: Cassava Mosaic Geminivirus (CMG) vectored by Bemisia tabaci
cassava mosaic.symptoms: Severe mosaic mottling with chlorotic pale yellow and green patches, leaflet distortion, puckering, and stunting of root tubers.
cassava mosaic.cultural: Use certified virus-free stem cuttings; rogue infected plants; plant resistant cassava varieties (e.g. Sree Padmanabha).
cassava mosaic.biological: Conserve whitefly natural enemies; spray neem oil.
cassava mosaic.chemical: Foliar spray of Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Diafenthiuron 50% WP (@ 1.2 g/L) to control whitefly vector.
cassava mosaic.management: Use virus-free disease-free stem cuttings. Spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (@ 0.3 ml/L) for whitefly control.

cassava brown spot.symptoms: Uniform circular brown spots with distinct dark margins on older lower cassava leaves.
cassava brown spot.cultural: Collect and destroy fallen leaf litter; ensure proper plant spacing.
cassava brown spot.chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (@ 2.5 g/L).
cassava brown spot.management: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (@ 2.5 g/L).

aphids.organism: Aphidoidea (Aphis gossypii, Myzus persicae, Lipaphis erysimi, Rhopalosiphum)
aphids.symptoms: Dense insect colonies clustering on tender shoot tips, buds, and leaf undersides; causes upward leaf curling, crinkling, stunted terminal growth; abundant secretion of clear sticky honeydew attracting thick black sooty mold fungus.
aphids.cultural: Install yellow sticky traps (@ 15-20/acre) at crop canopy level; avoid excessive vegetative nitrogen fertilization; balance irrigation.
aphids.biological: Conserve predatory ladybird beetles (Coccinella septempunctata), green lacewings (Chrysoperla carnea), and syrphid fly larvae; spray Verticillium lecanii (@ 5g/L) or Neem oil 1500 ppm (@ 3 ml/L).
aphids.chemical: Foliar spray of Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (@ 0.3 ml/L or 60 ml/acre) or Thiamethoxam 25% WG (@ 0.3 g/L or 60 g/acre) or Acetamiprid 20% SP (@ 0.2 g/L) or Flonicamid 50% WG (@ 0.3 g/L).
aphids.etl: 10-15 aphids per shoot or 10% infested plants.
aphids.management: Install yellow sticky traps (15/acre). Spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Thiamethoxam 25 WG (@ 0.3 g/L) or Flonicamid 50 WG (@ 0.3 g/L).

cicadellidae.organism: Cicadellidae (Leafhoppers, Jassids - Amrasca biguttula, Nephotettix virescens)
cicadellidae.symptoms: Nymphs and adults feed on leaf undersides, injecting toxic saliva: leaf margins turn yellow, curl downward, and become reddish-brown ('hopperburn'); vectors of destructive phytoplasmas and viruses.
cicadellidae.cultural: Install yellow sticky traps (@ 10-15/acre); maintain clean field borders free of alternate weeds; timely early sowing.
cicadellidae.biological: Conserve predatory mirid bugs (Cyrtorhinus) and spiders; spray Beauveria bassiana 1.15% WP (@ 5g/L) or NSKE 5%.
cicadellidae.chemical: Foliar spray of Dinotefuran 20% SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Flonicamid 50% WG (@ 0.3 g/L or 60 g/acre) or Thiamethoxam 25% WG (@ 0.3 g/L) or Diafenthiuron 50% WP (@ 1.2 g/L).
cicadellidae.etl: 1-2 jassids per leaf during vegetative phase.
cicadellidae.management: Install yellow sticky traps. Spray Dinotefuran 20 SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Flonicamid 50 WG (@ 0.3 g/L) or Thiamethoxam 25 WG (@ 0.3 g/L).

thrips.organism: Thripidae (Scirtothrips dorsalis, Thrips tabaci, Frankliniella schultzei)
thrips.symptoms: Silvery mottled or bleached patches with tiny dark fecal specks on leaf surfaces; leaf curling, crinkling of margins, and necrotic scarring on young fruit; major vector of Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus (TSWV) and Bud Necrosis.
thrips.cultural: Install blue sticky traps (@ 15/acre) at crop height; use silver reflective mulches; overhead sprinkler irrigation can wash thrips off plants.
thrips.biological: Conserve predatory minute pirate bugs (Orius spp.) and phytoseiid mites; spray Lecanicillium lecanii (@ 5g/L) or Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%).
thrips.chemical: Foliar spray of Spinosad 45% SC (@ 0.3 ml/L or 60 ml/acre) or Fipronil 5% SC (@ 2 ml/L or 400 ml/acre) or Spinetoram 11.7% SC (@ 0.5 ml/L) or Cyantraniliprole 10.26% OD (@ 1.2 ml/L).
thrips.management: Install blue sticky traps (15/acre). Spray Spinosad 45 SC (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Fipronil 5 SC (@ 2 ml/L) or Spinetoram 11.7 SC (@ 0.5 ml/L).

miridae.organism: Miridae (Plant Bugs / Capsid Bugs - Adelphocoris, Apolygus lucorum, Campylomma)
miridae.symptoms: Piercing-sucking feeding punctures produce small necrotic spots that drop out, creating ragged 'shot-holes' in expanding leaves; causes flower and square blighting and fruit shedding.
miridae.cultural: Eliminate broadleaf weeds on field margins; shake plants over white tray for early detection.
miridae.biological: Conserve predatory reduviid assassin bugs and spiders; spray Beauveria bassiana (@ 5g/L).
