miridae.chemical: Foliar spray of Flonicamid 50% WG (@ 0.3 g/L) or Thiamethoxam 25% WG (@ 0.3 g/L) or Clothianidin 50% WDG (@ 0.25 g/L).
miridae.etl: 1-2 mirid bugs per plant at flowering/bud stage.
miridae.management: Spray Flonicamid 50 WG (@ 0.3 g/L) or Thiamethoxam 25 WG (@ 0.3 g/L) if bugs exceed threshold during squaring.

army worm.organism: Spodoptera litura (Tobacco Caterpillar / Cutworm) & Spodoptera frugiperda
army worm.symptoms: Young larvae feed gregariously skeletonizing leaves; grown larvae devour entire leaves, petioles, and tender shoots nocturnal feeding, leaving plants completely defoliated overnight.
army worm.cultural: Deep summer plowing to expose pupae to predatory birds; install sex pheromone traps (@ 5 traps/acre); collection and destruction of golden egg masses and gregarious young larvae.
army worm.biological: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis (@ 1.5 lakh/ha); foliar spray of SlNPV (Spodoptera litura Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus @ 250 LE/ha) or Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt @ 2 g/L).
army worm.chemical: Foliar spray of Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG (@ 0.4 g/L or 80 g/acre) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Novaluron 10% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L) or Spinetoram 11.7% SC (@ 0.5 ml/L).
army worm.etl: 1 egg mass per 10 meters row or 1-2 larvae per plant.
army worm.management: Install pheromone traps (5/acre). Spray Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (@ 0.3 ml/L) during late evening hours.

beet army worm.symptoms: Larvae web leaves together and feed within, skeletonizing foliage and burrowing into crowns and fruit.
beet army worm.biological: Bt formulations (@ 2 g/L) or Spodoptera NPV.
beet army worm.chemical: Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Spinetoram 11.7% SC (@ 0.5 ml/L).
beet army worm.management: Spray Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Spinetoram 11.7 SC (@ 0.5 ml/L).

cabbage army worm.symptoms: Extensive leaf chewing and deep tunneling into brassica heads.
cabbage army worm.cultural: Summer plowing, hand collection of egg masses.
cabbage army worm.chemical: Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Flubendiamide 39.35% SC (@ 0.25 ml/L).
cabbage army worm.management: Spray Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Bt formulations.

black cutworm.symptoms: Nocturnal larvae cut young seedling stems right at the soil line, causing seedlings to fall over and wilt.
black cutworm.cultural: Deep plowing; keep fields weed-free 2 weeks before planting; place collar around seedling stems.
black cutworm.biological: Apply entomopathogenic nematodes (Steinernema carpocapsae) to soil.
black cutworm.chemical: Soil drenching around seedlings with Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 3 ml/L) or broadcast poison bait (Wheat bran 10 kg + Jaggery 1 kg + Chlorpyrifos 20 EC 500 ml).
black cutworm.management: Broadcast poison bait (bran + jaggery + Chlorpyrifos) in evening or drench seedling collar with Chlorpyrifos 20 EC (@ 3 ml/L).

large cutworm.symptoms: Severed stems at soil level, hollowed root crowns.
large cutworm.chemical: Poison bait or Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 3 ml/L).
large cutworm.management: Apply poison bait or soil drench around plant collars.

yellow cutworm.symptoms: Seedling cutting at ground level, root crown chewing.
yellow cutworm.management: Soil drench seedling rows with Chlorpyrifos 20 EC (@ 3 ml/L).

blister beetle.organism: Mylabris pustulata / Epicauta spp. - Meloid Blister Beetle
blister beetle.symptoms: Adult beetles feed voraciously on flowers, floral buds, and young tender pods of pulses, cotton, and vegetables, drastically reducing pod/fruit set.
blister beetle.cultural: Handpick adult beetles using protective rubber gloves in early morning when sluggish (beetles secrete cantharidin which blisters skin); light traps.
blister beetle.chemical: Dust field with Malathion 5% dust (@ 10 kg/acre) or foliar spray Quinalphos 25% EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 2.5 ml/L).
blister beetle.management: Handpick with gloves in early morning. Spray Quinalphos 25 EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Chlorpyrifos 20 EC (@ 2.5 ml/L).

legume blister beetle.symptoms: Voracious feeding on legume flowers, leading to total blossom drop.
legume blister beetle.cultural: Manual collection with gloves in morning; light traps.
legume blister beetle.chemical: Dust Malathion 5% dust or spray Quinalphos 25 EC (@ 2 ml/L).
legume blister beetle.management: Manual collection or spray Quinalphos 25 EC (@ 2 ml/L) during bloom.

red spider.symptoms: Fine yellow speckling or stippling on upper leaf surface, progressing to gray or bronze scorching; dense fine webbing covers leaf undersides and shoot tips under hot, dry conditions.
red spider.cultural: Avoid water stress; overhead sprinkler irrigation to knock down mite colonies; wash dust from crop borders.
red spider.biological: Conserve predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis, Neoseiulus californicus); spray Wettable Sulphur 80% WP (@ 2.5 g/L).
red spider.chemical: Foliar spray of Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (@ 1 ml/L or 200 ml/acre) or Propargite 57% EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Diafenthiuron 50% WP (@ 1.2 g/L) or Fenazaquin 10% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L).
red spider.etl: 5-10 mites per leaf or first fine webbing noticed.
red spider.management: Avoid dry conditions. Spray Spiromesifen 22.9 SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Propargite 57 EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Wettable Sulphur 80 WP (@ 2.5 g/L).

longlegged spider mite.symptoms: Mottled leaf yellowing, bronzing, and foliar desiccation during dry spells.
longlegged spider mite.chemical: Propargite 57 EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9 SC (@ 1 ml/L).
longlegged spider mite.management: Spray Spiromesifen 22.9 SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Wettable Sulphur 80 WP (@ 2.5 g/L).

aleurocanthus spiniferus.symptoms: Dense colonies of spiny black nymphs on leaf undersides, copious sticky honeydew fostering thick black sooty mold fungus covering canopy.
aleurocanthus spiniferus.cultural: Prune infested lower leaves, improve canopy airflow.
aleurocanthus spiniferus.biological: Release parasitic aphelinid wasps (Encarsia smithi); spray Neem oil 1500 ppm (@ 3 ml/L).
aleurocanthus spiniferus.chemical: Spray Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Pyriproxyfen 10% EC (@ 1.5 ml/L) or Acetamiprid 20% SP (@ 0.3 g/L).
aleurocanthus spiniferus.management: Release Encarsia parasitoids. Spray Spiromesifen 22.9 SC (@ 1 ml/L) or Acetamiprid 20 SP (@ 0.3 g/L).

trialeurodes vaporariorum.symptoms: Tiny white moth-like adults fluttering from leaf undersides when disturbed; yellow leaf chlorosis, stunted growth, sooty mold.
trialeurodes vaporariorum.cultural: Yellow sticky cards (@ 20/greenhouse); screen vents with 50-mesh insect netting.
trialeurodes vaporariorum.biological: Release Encarsia formosa wasps; spray Beauveria bassiana (@ 5g/L).
trialeurodes vaporariorum.chemical: Spray Flonicamid 50% WG (@ 0.3 g/L) or Diafenthiuron 50% WP (@ 1.2 g/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (@ 1 ml/L).
trialeurodes vaporariorum.management: Deploy yellow sticky traps. Spray Diafenthiuron 50 WP (@ 1.2 g/L) or Flonicamid 50 WG (@ 0.3 g/L).

flea beetle.symptoms: Adult beetles chew numerous tiny circular shot-holes through leaf blades; cotyledons and young leaves look peppered with holes.
flea beetle.cultural: Use insect exclusion netting on seedlings; keep beds weed-free.
flea beetle.biological: Spray Beauveria bassiana (@ 5g/L); apply neem cake.
flea beetle.chemical: Spray Thiamethoxam 25% WG (@ 0.3 g/L) or Cypermethrin 10% EC (@ 1 ml/L) or Deltamethrin 2.8% EC (@ 1 ml/L).
flea beetle.etl: 1 beetle per seedling or 10% leaf area chewed.
flea beetle.management: Install floating row covers. Spray Thiamethoxam 25 WG (@ 0.3 g/L) or Cypermethrin 10 EC (@ 1 ml/L).

grub.organism: Holotrichia consanguinea / H. serrata - White Grub (Scarab Beetle Larvae)
grub.symptoms: C-shaped whitish subterranean grubs chew tap roots and rootlets, causing sudden wilting, drying, and lodging of plants in patches across the field.
grub.cultural: Deep summer plowing to expose grubs to birds; install light traps (1/ha) after first pre-monsoon shower to kill adult beetles.
grub.biological: Soil application of entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium anisopliae or Beauveria brongniartii (@ 2.5 kg/ha enriched in FYM).
grub.chemical: Seed treatment with Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 6-10 ml/kg seed) or Fipronil 40% + Imidacloprid 40% WG (Lesenta @ 2-3 g/kg seed). Standing crop: drench with Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 4 ml/L) or apply Fipronil 0.3% GR (@ 10 kg/acre).
grub.management: Light traps for adult beetles. Soil drench with Chlorpyrifos 20 EC (@ 4 ml/L) or apply Fipronil 0.3 GR (@ 10 kg/acre).

mole cricket.symptoms: Nymphs and adults burrow underground, severing seedling roots, pushing up seedlings, and chewing plant crowns at night.
mole cricket.chemical: Broadcast poison bait (Rice bran 10 kg + Jaggery 1 kg + Chlorpyrifos 20 EC 500 ml) or soil drench Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 3 ml/L).
mole cricket.management: Broadcast poison bait in late evening or flood field to force crickets to surface.

wireworm.symptoms: Hard yellowish-brown cylindrical wireworms bore into planted seeds, germinating seedlings, and underground tubers, causing patchy stands.
wireworm.cultural: Rotate with non-susceptible crops (brassicas); deep summer plowing.
wireworm.chemical: Soil application of Fipronil 0.3% GR (@ 10 kg/acre) or seed dressing with Imidacloprid 70% WS (@ 4 g/kg seed).
wireworm.management: Apply Fipronil 0.3 GR (@ 10 kg/acre) in furrow at planting.

locustoidea.organism: Schistocerca gregaria / Locusta migratoria (Desert & Migratory Locust)
locustoidea.symptoms: Massive flying swarms strip every leaf, shoot, flower, and bark within hours, completely denuding entire fields.
locustoidea.cultural: Dig trenches to trap marching hopper bands; beat drums/create noise to prevent settling.
locustoidea.biological: Aerial spray of Metarhizium acridum (Green Muscle bio-pesticide).
locustoidea.chemical: Emergency control: ULV or barrier spraying of Malathion 96% ULV or Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 3-4 ml/L) or Deltamethrin 2.8% EC.
locustoidea.etl: Presence of gregarious locust hopper bands or swarms.
locustoidea.management: Alert local agriculture department / Locust Warning Organization (LWO). Spray Chlorpyrifos 20 EC (@ 3.5 ml/L) or Malathion.

dacus dorsalis.symptoms: Female punctures mature fruit to lay eggs; maggots feed inside pulp causing watery breakdown, premature yellowing, and fruit rotting with exit holes.
dacus dorsalis.cultural: Install Methyl Eugenol pheromone traps (@ 10 traps/ha); collect and bury fallen infested fruits in deep pits (at least 60 cm deep); fruit bagging.
dacus dorsalis.chemical: Bait spray application: Jaggery / Protein hydrolysate (100g) + Malathion 50% EC (20 ml) in 10 L water, sprayed in coarse droplets on tree canopies.
dacus dorsalis.management: Install Methyl Eugenol traps (10/ha). Spray bait mixture (Jaggery + Malathion) on trunk and lower canopy.

alfalfa seed chalcid.symptoms: Larvae feed and develop entirely inside growing legume seeds; adult emerges through a tiny circular exit hole, leaving hollow lightweight empty seed pods.
alfalfa seed chalcid.cultural: Synchronize blooming and seed harvest across the area; eliminate volunteer host legumes along borders; burn chaff.
alfalfa seed chalcid.biological: Conserve pteromalid parasitoid wasps; spray neem extract.
alfalfa seed chalcid.chemical: Foliar spray of Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Quinalphos 25% EC (@ 2 ml/L) before peak seed oviposition.
alfalfa seed chalcid.management: Synchronize harvest and spray Quinalphos 25 EC (@ 2 ml/L) before peak pod setting.

alfalfa weevil.symptoms: Larvae chew holes in tender terminal foliage, skeletonizing leaves giving field a frosted, bleached white appearance.
alfalfa weevil.cultural: Early cutting / harvesting of first hay crop to starve larvae; field grazing in winter.
alfalfa weevil.biological: Conserve Bathyplectes parasitoid wasps; spray Beauveria bassiana (@ 5g/L).
alfalfa weevil.chemical: Spray Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Lambdacyhalothrin 5% EC (@ 0.5 ml/L) or Malathion 50% EC (@ 2 ml/L).
alfalfa weevil.etl: 1-2 larvae per stem or 30-40% damaged stems.
alfalfa weevil.management: Early harvest or spray Lambdacyhalothrin 5 EC (@ 0.5 ml/L) if 30% stems damaged.

soybean diabrotica speciosa.organism: Diabrotica speciosa - Cucurbit Beetle / Chrysomelid Leaf Beetle
soybean diabrotica speciosa.symptoms: Adults chew irregular holes in foliage and feed on flower petals; larvae feed on root nodules and taproots leading to plant lodging.
soybean diabrotica speciosa.cultural: Crop rotation with non-host crops; install yellow sticky monitoring traps; balanced nutrition.
soybean diabrotica speciosa.biological: Foliar spray of Beauveria bassiana (@ 5g/L) or Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%).
soybean diabrotica speciosa.chemical: Foliar spray of Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Lambdacyhalothrin 5% EC (@ 0.5 ml/L) or Thiamethoxam 25% WG (@ 0.3 g/L).
soybean diabrotica speciosa.etl: 2-3 beetles per meter row or 20% defoliation.
soybean diabrotica speciosa.management: Rotate crops. Spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (@ 0.3 ml/L) or NSKE 5%.

soybean caterpillar.organism: Anticarsia gemmatalis / Spodoptera litura - Soybean Defoliator
soybean caterpillar.symptoms: Larvae feed voraciously on soybean leaf blades, stripping foliage down to midribs and chewing into pods.
soybean caterpillar.biological: Nomuraea rileyi bio-fungicide or Bt (@ 2 g/L).
soybean caterpillar.chemical: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (@ 0.3 ml/L) or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG (@ 0.4 g/L).
soybean caterpillar.management: Spray Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (@ 0.3 ml/L).

adristyrannus.symptoms: Larvae chew irregular holes and skeletonize agricultural foliage during nocturnal feeding periods.
adristyrannus.cultural: Install light/pheromone traps; handpick egg masses.
adristyrannus.biological: Apply Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt @ 2 g/L) or Spinosad 45% SC on young larval instars.
adristyrannus.chemical: Chlorpyrifos 20% EC (@ 2 ml/L) or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG (@ 0.4 g/L).
adristyrannus.management: Deploy light traps. Spray Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG (@ 0.4 g/L) or Bt (@ 2 g/L).

blueberry.symptoms: Visible pathological lesions, chlorosis, and necrotic patterns consistent with blueberry on Crop foliage.
blueberry.cultural: Practice strict field hygiene, eliminate weed hosts around field edges, and ensure balanced fertilization and scheduled drip irrigation.
blueberry.biological: Seed/soil application of Trichoderma viride (@ 2.5 kg/ha) or foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens (@ 5g/L).
blueberry.chemical: Foliar spray of broad-spectrum protective fungicide Mancozeb 75% WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or systemic Difenoconazole 25% EC (@ 0.5 ml/L). Consult your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK).
blueberry.etl: First appearance of expanding lesions in field.
blueberry.management: Inspect Crop canopy. Remove affected leaves and spray Mancozeb 75 WP (@ 2.5 g/L) or Difenoconazole 25 EC (@ 0.5 ml/L).

ampelophaga.cultural: Erect sticky traps (yellow/blue @ 15/acre), clean field margins, and monitor light traps.
ampelophaga.biological: Foliar spray of 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Beauveria bassiana 1.15% WP (@ 5g/L).
ampelophaga.chemical: Foliar spray of selective contact/systemic insecticide: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (@ 0.3 ml/L) for chewers, or Thiamethoxam 25% WG (@ 0.3 g/L) for sucking pests. Consult local KVK.
ampelophaga.etl: When insect count exceeds regional economic threshold level.
ampelophaga.management: Deploy sticky traps. Apply NSKE 5% or targeted spray of Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (@ 0.3 ml/L).
